question.worked_solution:
If $Z∼N(0,1),$ then by the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

Also, since $Z$ is continuous, 

$$
P(Z<-0.36)=P(Z\le -0.36)=Φ(-0.36).
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14254773/assets/06ab72c4b54e672a81892dbb8e7193dec7dc6d75b9b13bfcd1abe7286211a4a5.png)

Now, we determine the value of $Φ(-0.36)$ from the table:

- We first select the row that corresponds to $-0.3$ and the column that corresponds to $0.06.$

- Then, we take the value that lies at the intersection:

| $z$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-0.4\,$ | $\,0.3264\,$ | $\,0.3228\,$ | $\,0.3192\,$ |
| $\,-0.3\,$ | $\,0.3632\,$ | $\,0.3594\,$ | $\,0.3557\,$ |
| $\,-0.2\,$ | $\,0.4013\,$ | $\,0.3974\,$ | $\,0.3936\,$ |

Therefore, according to the table, we have

$$
P(Z\le -0.36)=Φ(-0.36)=0.3594.
$$
